title: Phosphoproteome analysis of BRK1-stimulated endothelial cells
projectDescription: Identification of BRK1's downstream signaling targets.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Human coronary artery endothelial cells (HCAECs, 1.2 × 10^6 cells per replicate)) were stimulated with BRK1 (100 ng / ml) or VEGFA (25 ng / ml) for 15 min. HCAECs were solubilized in urea buffer containing cOmplete Mini protease inhibitor cocktail (Roche) and PhosSTOP (Roche). After trypsin-digestion, phosphopeptides were enriched (Pierce, TiO2 and Fe-NTA phosphopeptide enrichment kits, catalog numbers A32993 and A32992) and fractionated (Pierce, High pH Reversed Phase Peptide Fractionation Kit, catalog number 84868). Five fractions per replicate and condition were reconstituted in HPLC loading buffer.
dataProcessingProtocol: Generated spectra were analyzed with MaxQuant 1.6.17, applying the integrated Andromeda search engine against the UniProt knowledgebase. Phosphorylation (S/T/Y), oxidation (M), deamidation (N/Q), and N-terminal acetylation were set as variable modifications; carbamidomethylation (C) was set as fixed modification. Potential contaminants, reverse database hits, and phosphopeptides with a localization probability below 0.75 were excluded. Phosphosites not detectable in all four replicates from at least one experimental condition were filtered out. Missing values were imputed based on the normal distribution of all measured log2-transformed intensities using Perseus 1.6.14, applying a width of 0.3 and a downshift of 1.8 separately for each replicate.
